title: Two Hundred Tasks for a Quiet Night
description:
> **Who is asking**
>
> **Analytics** (Helix). They run a small overnight aggregate for a QA board. The logic is trivial. The stage graph looks busy. The clock disagrees with how little data there is.

**Run night:** `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` is left large (e.g. 200) on a tiny dataset — hundreds of near-empty tasks; scheduling overhead dominates.

**Submit night (when live):** partitions may be set too low on a larger drop so each task is huge. Same skill: right-size shuffle partitions for the data.

## Your task

1. Run the planted aggregate. Open the shuffle stage.
2. Investigation: how many tasks, roughly how much data per task, too many or too few.
3. Set a sane shuffle partition count for this workload (lasting conf or job-local).
4. Re-run under the time budget with correct output.

## Rules

- Do not change the business logic of the aggregate.
- Do not enable AQE (coalesce would cheat the lesson).
- Do not add executors as the primary fix.
- Do not shrink input to make it fast.

> **Done when**
>
> Correct aggregate, partitions appropriate to the planted night, time budget met.

**Runners and datasets ship later.** You can open the workspace and read the brief; Run/Submit are not graded yet.

hints: AQE stays off for this chapter.
Fill Investigation before you call the job done.
Live Start ships when the lab is finalized.
